inspection of the cartridge shall be in accordance with IS : 2500 3. Sampling - The acceptance the (Part 1)-l 973 `Inspection by attributes and by count of defects ( first revision )`. A list showing classification of defects and AQLS to be adopted is given in Appendix A. 4. Tests 4.1 Drop Test - Ten capped cases shall be dropped through a distance of 244 cm in a suitable drop test apparatus, The capped cases should be securely held in adopter in a 30 kg block with mouths of No cap shall function after dropping. half the cases downward and the remaining with mouth upward. 4.2 Sensitivity TestTwenty five capped cartridge cases from each lot shall be tested for sensitivity in cap test apparatus, using a carbon steel ball weighing exactly 113'4 g and adjusted to give a drop of 30 cm. All the caps (sensitivity tested) shall fire satisfactorily under these conditions. 4.3 Insensitivity Test - Twenty proof samples shall be selected from each lot and assembled into cartridge cases. Then these cases shall be tested for insensitivity in the sensitivity test apparatus using suitable adopter and carbon steel ball weighing 113'4 g to give a drop of IO.00 cm; none of the cap shall function. 4.4 Case Proof-Twenty random sample cases from each case lot shall be subjected to the case proof by filling up with 10 percent extra charge mass of the propellant than assessed and subjected to the functioning and casuality tests and inspected for the defects mentioned in B-1.2(e) except for SI No. 11 and sentenced as follows: AQL Critical Major Minor 0 0'65 1'5 2

4.5 Pull Off Test for Head and BodyFive cartridge cases from each lot shall be tested for the The value so tested shall strength of holding between head and the tube using a suitable apparatus. not be less than 784 N ( 80 kg ) in single case and average 833 N ( 85 kg ) for general purpose and not less than 833 N ( 85 kg ) in single case and average 882 N ( 90 kg ) for competition cartridges. 4.6 Pull Off of Turnover ( for General Purpose Cartridges ) - Five cartridges from each lot shall be tested for the strength of turn over closure by cutting open as near to the head as possible and the The individual value of the strength of closure shall contents removed without disturbing the closure. not be less than 156'8 N ( 16 kg ) and not more than 274 N ( 28 kg ). 4.7 Pull Off of Crimp Closure for Competition Cartridges - Five cartridges from each lot shall be tested for the strength of crimp closure by cutting open as near to the head as possible and the contents The individual value of the strength of closure shall not be removed without disturbing the closure. less than 156.8 N ( 16 kg ) and not more than 274 N ( 28 kg ). 4.8 4.9

5. Re-submission of Rejected Batches - Rejected batches may be re-submitted with the approval of the purchaser. Where re-submission is permitted and the manufacturer elects to resubmit, the manufacturer shall first inspect the rejected lot, either for the particular types or classes of defects that caused the batch to be rejected, or for all types and classes of defects, and directed by the purchaser. The manufacturer shall repair or remove all defectives of these types of classes. The purchaser shall inspect a re-submitted batch for the types or classes of defects, using normal or tightened inspection at his discretion. 6. Packing and Marking - The cartridges shall be delivered in the lot of 10 000 or 50 000 plus cartridges of proof as mentioned in Appendix B. However, whenever a propellant is changed, a separate cartridge lot is to be started. 6.1 Twenty cartons containing 25 cartridges per carton shall be packed in one box or as specified in the contract or order but overall mass of one packed box shall not exceed 35 kg for safety in handling. 6.2 Cartridges and boxes and cartons shall be marked/stencilled suitably and/or trade-mark and the words `Shot Gun Cartgs' and `Made in India'. 6.3 Standard

Safety - Responsibility for the safety of operation rests with the manufacturer and guidelines for safe usage provided by the manufacturer are followed properly.

A-l .2 Critical Defect - Which according to judgement and experience is likely to result in hazardous or unsafe condition for individuals using, maintaining or depending upon the product or which is likely to prevent performance of the tactical function of a weapon. A-l.3 Major Defect - That is likely to result in failure, or to reduce materially product for its intended purpose; excludes critical defects. the usability of the unit of

A-l .4 Minor Defect - That is not likely to reduce materially the usability of unit of product for its intended purpose, or is a departure from established standards having little bearing on the effective use or operation of the unit. A-2. Examination defects. shall be

EXPLANATORY

NOTE
requirements

This Indian Standard is being issued in the following parts, Part 1 covering general for shot gun plastic cartridges and subsequent parts covering the plastic components: Part 1 General requirements Part 2 Blank cartridges Part 3 Plastic body tube Part 4 Plastic base wad Part 5 Plastic power piston
